note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 85; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 12) on data/benches/qualitative.json: an unknown salt's ions by their tests and the flame.
title: Experiment: what is in it?

report.label: its cation
report.why: Sodium hydroxide tells copper (blue) and iron(III) (rust brown); the flame the rest: sodium yellow, lithium crimson, calcium orange-red, barium green.

report.label: its anion
report.why: White in tube 1 is chloride, white in tube 2 sulfate, bubbles in tube 3 carbonate; a nitrate answers none of them.

steps.title: Four samples of the unknown
steps.text: Pick up the unknown, right-click tube 1, type 3 and click "pour". The same into tubes 2, 3 and 4.
steps.why: Each test takes its own sample: what one test adds would spoil the next.

steps.title: Chloride: silver nitrate
steps.text: Pick up the silver nitrate, right-click tube 1, type 1 and click "pour". A white solid means chloride: silver chloride.
steps.why: The nitric acid in it keeps carbonate and hydroxide from bringing silver out as well: only the halides stay solid in acid.

steps.title: Sulfate: barium chloride
steps.text: Pick up the barium chloride, right-click tube 2, type 1 and click "pour". A white solid means sulfate: barium sulfate.
steps.why: In acid, barium carbonate does not form: only the sulfate comes out.

steps.title: Carbonate: acid
steps.text: Pick up the hydrochloric acid, right-click tube 3, type 1 and click "pour". Bubbles mean carbonate: its carbon dioxide.

steps.title: Sodium hydroxide
steps.text: Pick up the sodium hydroxide, right-click tube 4, type 1 and click "pour". Blue: copper(II) hydroxide. Rust brown: iron(III) hydroxide. Nothing, or a little white: look to the flame.

steps.title: Light the burner
steps.text: Right-click the burner and drag its valve open.

steps.title: The flame test
steps.text: Pick up the unknown and click the burner: a loop dipped in it is held in the flame. Watch the flame's colour. You can do it again: its colour lasts a few seconds.
steps.why: Each metal's atoms, heated in the flame, give out light at their own lines: sodium's yellow at 589 nm, lithium's crimson at 671, calcium's and barium's the bands of their hydroxides, orange-red and green.
